timeline.shipped: Company and competitor research; three prototype concepts
MCP server spec with OAuth design and junk-draft guardrails
Dropped MCP for a no-setup browser demo (reviewers won't connect an AI tool). Dropped the AI-review idea after finding Submittable already ships Smart Reviewer. Wrote this spec.

Repo initialized and pushed to GitHub (github.com/pauljmillar/program-builder). Next.js App Router + TypeScript + Tailwind scaffold. Design tokens and free font substitutes (EB Garamond, Inter, JetBrains Mono) wired in. Page shells for /, /why, /build-log, /how-it-works. CI workflow (lint, typecheck, build), green on main. First production deploy to Vercel (program-builder-gamma.vercel.app), connected to the GitHub repo for auto-deploy on push.

Zod schema for the full program (lib/schema.ts) with JSON Schema export via zod's native toJSONSchema. estimateMinutes formula. All 10 checker rules from spec §6 (lib/validate/rules/*), each with a passing and a breaking Vitest case. Added pnpm test to CI.

Sequential 7-step generation pipeline (lib/generate), one Claude tool-use call per section, versioned prompts (lib/prompts/v1), and the checker + repair loop (max 2 rounds). `pnpm build-program "<prompt>"` runs it end to end. Verified with two real API calls: a clean sample prompt (zero issues on the first pass) and a deliberately contradictory one ("$10,000 fund... awards up to $50,000") that correctly left an unresolvable PROMPT_CONFLICT in `remaining` after 2 repair rounds, rather than silently picking a number.

pnpm record generates the 3 real samples in content/samples/*.json (actual API calls, no fabricated output). Replay UI: StepList, SectionCard, CheckCard, ProgramTabs (Program/JSON/In Submittable), and per-section renderers, orchestrated by ProgramDemo, which replays each sample using its real recorded per-step timings. All 3 samples passed every checker rule on the first try (see finding above) rather than needing a repair-round catch.

tools.usedFor: Scaffold, schema, checker, generation pipeline, UI, eval harness, deployment

failures.title: CI failed on first push: conflicting pnpm versions
failures.whatHappened: The CI workflow pinned `pnpm/action-setup@v4` to version 10 while package.json's `packageManager` field pinned pnpm@10.32.1. pnpm's own version check treats those as two different sources of truth and refuses to run.
failures.howCaught: First GitHub Actions run on main failed immediately in the 'Run pnpm/action-setup@v4' step, before lint/typecheck/build even started.
failures.fix: Dropped the explicit `version: 10` from the workflow step so action-setup reads the version from package.json's packageManager field instead.
failures.lesson: When package.json already pins a packageManager version, don't also pin it in CI config — pick one source of truth.

failures.title: CI typecheck failed: Next.js's generated route types weren't there yet
failures.whatHappened: `app/layout.tsx` uses Next.js's typed-routes `LayoutProps<'/'>` global, which only exists once Next.js has generated `.next/types` (gitignored). CI ran a standalone `tsc --noEmit` before anything had generated those types, so it failed on `Cannot find name 'LayoutProps'` even though `pnpm build` passed fine locally (build generates the types itself first).
failures.howCaught: Second CI run still failed, now in the typecheck step specifically, right after fixing the pnpm version issue.
failures.fix: Added a `next typegen` step before `pnpm typecheck` in CI, which generates just the route types without a full build.
failures.lesson: A typed-routes feature means `tsc --noEmit` alone isn't a complete typecheck in CI — it depends on a generation step that `next build`/`next dev` normally does implicitly.

failures.title: PROMPT_CONFLICT checker misread its own award-amount match as the fund total
failures.whatHappened: The PROMPT_CONFLICT rule's regex extraction scans every "$X" mention for nearby words like "fund" or "total" to guess the stated funding total. It didn't exclude mentions already claimed by the award-amount regexes ("up to $X", a "$X-$Y" range), so a prompt like "A fund for nonprofits. Awards up to $25,000" misread the award figure as the fund total too, because the word "fund" fell inside that mention's context window.
failures.howCaught: Unit test for PROMPT_CONFLICT (tests/unit/promptConflict.test.ts): a case asserting the award-max mismatch message contained both the expected and actual numbers failed because the extractor also fired a false fundingTotal mismatch, producing the wrong message at index 0.
failures.fix: Tracked the index ranges already claimed by award-amount matches and skip any money mention inside those ranges when scanning for a fund total.
failures.lesson: A regex-based extractor needs to track which spans of text it's already consumed, or a second heuristic pass will double-count the same number under a different label.

failures.title: First live API calls rejected the tool schema and the forced tool_choice
failures.whatHappened: Three real 400s from the Anthropic API on the first live run of the generation pipeline: (1) zod's exclusiveMinimum keyword (from `.positive()`) isn't supported in a tool's input_schema; (2) setting `strict: true` on the tool turned on a much more restricted schema subset that rejected even plain `minimum`; (3) with strict mode removed, the forced `tool_choice: {type: "tool", name}` itself came back "not supported for this model."
failures.howCaught: Running `pnpm build-program` against a real sample prompt with a real API key, per spec §0.7 — not caught by any unit test, since those don't hit the live API.
failures.fix: Changed `.positive()` to `.min(1)` in lib/schema.ts, dropped `strict: true` from the tool definition, and dropped the forced tool_choice entirely (tool_choice defaults to "auto", and with exactly one tool offered the model calls it every time in practice).
failures.lesson: The SDK's types don't tell you which JSON Schema keywords or tool_choice modes a given model actually accepts — that only shows up by calling the real API. Budget for this on any new model or SDK version.

failures.title: pnpm record failed on a real sample: the model sent a number as a quoted string
failures.whatHappened: The first real `pnpm record` run failed with a ZodError: `expectedApplications` came back from the model as the string "100" instead of the number 100, which `z.number()` correctly rejects. Nothing in the tool's JSON Schema forbids a numeric string, and the model treated it as an acceptable way to write the number.
failures.howCaught: Running the actual sample-recording script against the live API, not a unit test — the test fixtures only ever construct well-typed objects directly.
failures.fix: Switched every model-drafted numeric field in lib/schema.ts from `z.number()` to `z.coerce.number()` (fundingTotal, awardMin, awardMax, expectedApplications, maxWords, weight, order, reviewersPerApplication, panelSize, estimatedMinutes). Confirmed the JSON Schema output is unchanged (still `type: "number"`) and that it still correctly rejects non-numeric strings.
failures.lesson: A model filling in a JSON Schema's `type: "number"` can still hand back a numeric-looking string. Coerce at the validation boundary rather than trusting the type the schema asked for.

failures.title: The 3 canonical samples pass every check on the first try — no fabricated "catch" added
failures.whatHappened: The spec's demo mock-up shows the climate fund sample catching and fixing a rubric problem. In practice, across multiple real recordings (including a manual retry), all 3 canonical sample prompts (climate fund, Kestrel County, Northwind scholarship) generate clean on the first pass: zero errors, zero warnings, nothing for the repair loop to do.
failures.howCaught: `pnpm record` and a manual rerun of the climate-fund prompt, both against the live API.
failures.fix: Did not invent or inject an issue to force a "catch" moment, per spec §0.3 (never fabricate results). Left the Check card able to show a clean pass as a good outcome ("Passed every check on the first pass"). The real catch-and-repair demonstration lives in the eval set's deliberately-contradictory cases instead — verified directly with a test prompt ("$10,000 fund... awards up to $50,000"), where the checker correctly left an unresolved PROMPT_CONFLICT after 2 repair rounds rather than silently picking a number.
failures.lesson: A strong model with well-scoped prompts will often just get well-posed inputs right the first time — the checker's value shows up on messier or contradictory input, not on hand-picked clean demo prompts. Don't force a canned failure into a demo that doesn't naturally have one.

beforeProduction: Integration with the real Submittable V4 API behind a feature flag, with contract tests
Human review of generated rubrics for fairness and plain language before customer use
An eval set built from real (anonymized) customer programs, run in CI on every prompt or model change, with a release gate
Tracking edit distance: how much admins change each AI section, as the main quality signal
Prompt-injection tests (program descriptions that try to override instructions)
Observability: traces per step (latency, tokens, repair rounds), alerts on cost per program and pass-rate drops
Accessibility review of generated forms (labels, help text, reading level)
Per-tenant spend limits and model fallback
